en: The Scripture on the Buddha’s Teaching on the Extinction of Darkness in the Ten Directions, in one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Dharmarakṣa of the Yuezhi Kingdom during the Western Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was traveling among the Śākya monasteries in Kapilavastu.
Beneath the *kūṭaja* tree, he was together with a great assembly of bhikṣus—twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus—and an incalculable number of bodhisattvas.
At dawn, the Buddha donned his robes, took up his alms bowl, and, surrounded by his retinue of bhikṣus, entered the city to beg for food.
At that time, there was a young youth of the Śākya clan named Sunetra, who had prepared his carriage and departed from the city early in the morning.

From afar, he saw the World-Honored One together with the assembly of noble ones approaching; having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he alighted from his vehicle and proceeded on foot. He prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, Sunakṣatra was dejected and bowed his head in sorrow. The Buddha, knowing this through his supernormal knowledge, asked him:
"Young man, you departed from the city early this morning with a heart burning with anxiety and a countenance full of grief."
Mianshuai addressed the Buddha with a joyful countenance, saying:
“O God among Gods! Now my two parents are unwell;
they are being needlessly harassed by both humans and non-humans, finding no rest day or night whether awake or asleep, and even their coming and going or walking about are beset by distress.”

Furthermore, although my body dwells within a great kingdom, I have encountered such distress, poverty, and wretchedness; I reflect in secret, not knowing what plan to adopt, and I wonder what kind of expedient means I should employ?
Should we encounter hostile bandits, or meet with non-humans, malevolent spirits, or treacherous evils, there would be no means of protection.
We only pray that the World-Honored One will instruct us with the Dharma and provide timely rescue, so that we may be free from harm and affliction.
The Buddha told Sunakṣatra:
"Listen attentively!
Receive this with careful heed!"
"Maintain this with a virtuous mind, and I shall explain for you the method of protection.
At that time, the young boy Śakra received the instruction and listened.
The Buddha said:

"To the east, passing beyond eight thousand nayutas of Buddha-lands from here, there is a world named *Sarvāsravakṣaya* (Extinguishing All Defilements). Its Buddha is named *Samacaryā Tathāgata*, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there preaching the Dharma."

If a person travels toward the east, they should first prostrate, take refuge, and make offerings to the Buddhas of the eastern direction; then they will have no fear, and none will dare to harass them.

Whatever they wish to travel or undertake shall all be fulfilled according to their wishes; their resolve will never be disturbed, and whatever they contemplate in their minds will immediately be accomplished.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
"First pay homage to the Most Perfectly Awakened One, the Great Sage of Equal Practice;
only then, as you travel toward the east, will you be free from fear."
The Buddha told the youth:

"To the south, passing beyond ten billion hundred thousand buddha-fields from here, there is a world named *Samantamukhapramocana-vimala-prabhāsa*. Its Buddha is named *Prathamacittotpādabhayanirvṛtti-samudgataśīrṣa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha*, who currently dwells there preaching the Dharma."

If you wish to travel south, you should from afar prostrate and take refuge in that Buddha; only then should you set out. With single-minded devotion, keeping your thoughts focused on the Buddha without distraction, you will be free from fear and encounter no calamities.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
"Having already abandoned all manifold perceptions, the youth should practice this.
If he travels toward the south, he shall no longer encounter fear."
The Buddha told the youth:

"To the west of here, as many buddha-fields away as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, there is a world named Suviśeṣa. Its Buddha is named Vajrapadavikrāmin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells there preaching the Dharma."

If you wish to travel westward, you should first discourse upon and contemplate the Dharma of primordial purity, which is forever beyond perception, without arising or ceasing, and serenely pure. You should first prostrate and pay homage to that Buddha, taking refuge with single-minded devotion, and only then set forth; thus you will be free from fear and shall not encounter calamities or hardships.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
"All phenomena are without arising, And likewise without cessation;
One who understands this clearly Shall be free from fear."
The Buddha told the youth:

"To the north, passing from here beyond twenty thousand buddha-fields, there is a world named Bodhivibhāṣa. Its Buddha is named Ratnajñānaśikhin Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there preaching the Dharma."

If you wish to travel north, even while remaining at home, you should prostrate yourself, pay homage, and take refuge in that Buddha; only then should you set out, for you will then be free from fear and encounter no calamities.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
"If one remains within the home, regarding all household affairs and whatever possessions one carries northward, then there shall be no fear or dread."
The Buddha told the youth:

"To the northeast, passing from here through more than a hundred thousand million buddha-fields, there is a world named Sustaining What Is Contemplated. Its Buddha is named Destroyer of Mara’s Pride, Solitary Walker Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma."

Furthermore, when that Tathāgata approached the foot of the Bodhi tree and sat down with single-minded concentration, he transformed all the retinues of Māras and the celestial Māras throughout the trichiliocosm, exhorting them all to establish themselves in non-retrogression so that they would surely attain the unsurpassed, true, and correct path.
This is what moves [beings] when the Tathāgata approaches the foot of the tree.
If he proceeds toward the northeast, one should from afar prostrate and take refuge in that Buddha; only then should one advance. Wherever one goes, one will obtain peace and be without fear.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
"From the very first arousal of the thought of enlightenment, One has already subdued the armies of Māra.
If one constantly keeps this Buddha in mind, One will immediately be free from fear."
The Buddha told the youth:

"To the southeast, passing from here through as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in two Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Constantly Radiant. Its Buddha is named First Resolve, Non-retrogressive Wheel-Perfecting Chief Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells there preaching the Dharma."

When that Tathāgata was originally a bodhisattva, he constantly gave rise to the meaning of the non-retrogressive wheel through manifold practices: generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, undisturbed meditative concentration, and the accomplishment of wisdom.
This was moved by the Tathāgata when he was originally a bodhisattva.
If one travels toward the southeast, one should first prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground and single-mindedly take refuge; only then should one proceed, and thus there will be no fear.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
"First perform prostrations with the five limbs, and only then go forth into homelessness;
wherever you may travel while still in the realm of desire, you shall not encounter harm from bandits."
The Buddha told the youth:

"To the southwest, passing beyond eighty thousand buddha-fields from here, there is a world named Covered with White Interlaced Jewels. Its Buddha is named Jewel Canopy Illuminating the Void Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there preaching the Dharma."

If you travel toward the southwest, you should first prostrate to the Tathāgata of that direction, scatter flowers from afar while contemplating signlessness, and only then proceed; thus, you will be free from fear.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
“Those who make offerings to the Samyaksaṃbuddha, Scattering flowers as an act of veneration,
With a mind free from marks (animitta), Shall have no fear.”
The Buddha told the youth:

"To the northwest, passing from here through buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of six Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Abiding in Purity. Its Buddha is named Kaihua Pusa (Awakening and Transforming Bodhisattva) Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently resides there preaching the Dharma."
That Buddha-land is pure and free from defilement; it is devoid of craving and desire, has no women, and is removed from the five sensual pleasures.

If one travels toward the northwest, first pays homage to that Buddha, takes refuge, repents of one’s transgressions, and purely cultivates the Brahma-faring life before renouncing the household life, then one will be free from fear.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
"First one should cultivate pure conduct, and only then leave the home life;
thus remaining secure and not encountering bandits, one will face no manifold difficulties wherever one goes."
The Buddha told the youth:

"Below this world, past ninety-two *koṭis* of Buddha-fields, there is a world named *Smṛty-aviparyāsa*. Its Buddha is named *Smṛti-prathama-cittotpāda-saṃśaya-cchedana-kāma-niḥsaraṇa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha*, who is currently present preaching the Dharma."

Whether when you wish to sit or when you lie down at night, recollect this Tathāgata and pay homage with self-surrender; always contemplate saving sentient beings with universal compassion. Only then should you sit or lie down; thus you will be free from fear, and whatever you wish for will surely be fulfilled.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
“With universal compassion mindful of all sentient beings, Whether sitting in meditation or lying down to sleep,
Whether dreaming or awake, One shall have no fear.”
The Buddha told the youth:

"To the north, passing from here through as many buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in sixty Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Free from All Fear and Without Abode. Its Buddha is named King Who Surpasses and Equalizes the Elimination of Darkness, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells there preaching the Dharma."

If you rise from your seat, always pay homage to that Buddha, take refuge in him, and make offerings to him; always maintain a mind of loving-kindness and compassion for all sentient beings before rising to act, then you will be free from fear. Wherever you go or whatever you undertake, you will obtain auspicious peace and security. By virtue of this mindfulness, you will always receive protection.
The Buddha then spoke in verse:
"Always harboring a mind of equanimity and loving-kindness, Compassionating all classes of sentient beings—
Because one pities the multitude of living creatures, One shall have no fear."
The Buddha told the youth:
"You should receive these names of the Buddhas with careful attention; uphold them, contemplate them, and cherish them in your heart. Then, wherever you wish to go, there shall be no peril."
The youth of the Śākya clan, with a serene and joyful countenance, stepped forward before the Buddha and said:

"I have already received these names of the Buddhas; I hold them in my heart, contemplate them, and shall practice accordingly. Their matters are immeasurable, and having established this resolve within my own mind, I perceive the ten directions without any obstruction."
"Now, that which the World-Honored One has just spoken—proclaiming the Way of the sutras and the names of the various Buddhas—is exactly as we have heard it; it is precise and without discrepancy.

At that time, the assembly, numbering a full hundred thousand people, having heard what the Buddha had said, all rose from their seats, adjusted their robes, knelt with their right knees on the ground, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, whose great compassion universally covers all, you have now preached this sutra for our sake."
“I and all others see all the Buddhas; inside and out, everything is transparent and there is no darkness or obscuration. It is exactly as the Buddha has said, without any difference.
Thereupon, Śāriputra came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How swift is the purification of the eyes attained by these sons of good family! To behold all the Buddhas without any obstruction—how great indeed is the power of their merit!”
"Is this due to being sustained by the majestic spiritual power of these Buddhas,
or is it brought about by the merit and blessings of my own past lives?
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"This is due to the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, as well as his original merit.

At that time, the Buddha emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated the ten directions; the earth shook violently, the heavens scattered flowers and incense, and lutes and musical instruments resounded spontaneously without being struck.
The worthy Ānanda immediately rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"For what reason now does this great radiance appear, illuminating everything without exception, while the earth trembles violently and the heavens scatter flowers and incense?"
The Buddha said to Ānanda,
“Do you see those hundreds of thousands of people who stand before the Buddha with palms joined in homage?
Ānanda replied:
“I have seen them,
World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:

“By means of the roots of virtue established through these practices, these one hundred thousand people shall not fall into the evil realms for incalculable kalpas; each shall successively pass through worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, becoming wheel-turning sage kings who rule over the four continents.”

Alternatively, the Holy King shall constantly behold all Buddhas and attain the fulfillment of his own vows as he desires; thereafter, he shall achieve Buddhahood in this world, receiving the titles Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, and Bhagavat—all sharing these same names yet each attaining the Way in their own distinct realms.

As soon as the Buddha had conferred this prediction of enlightenment upon these sons of good family, the earth deities and the deities of the void simultaneously raised their voices in unison and proclaimed:
"The merit of these sons of good family is immeasurable."

That sound then reached the Four Heavenly Kings, the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and the Paranirmitavaśavartin Heaven, extending even to the realm of Māra; it ascended above to the Brahma Heaven and up to the twenty-fourth heaven, Akaniṣṭha, where all together sang in praise:
"Incomparable! Incomparable!"
How truly marvelous!
The majestic grace of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, is so capable of salvation; how sublime and magnificent it is!

They exhort and manifest transformation for the sons of noble families, bestowing upon them the prediction that they shall attain the unsurpassed, true, and right path, their wisdom being unimpeded and universally perceiving all things with complete success.
The youth of the Śākya clan, with a serene and joyful countenance, stepped forward and addressed the Buddha,
saying: "What is the title of this sutra,
and how should it be upheld?"
The Buddha told the youth:
"This sutra is titled 'Extinguishing the Darkness of the Ten Directions. Why is this so? Because..."

Recalling the Buddhas of the ten directions and taking refuge with single-minded devotion, the heart becomes tranquil as if seeing light in the darkness; no longer is there any fear. For this reason, it is called "Extinguishing the Darkness of the Ten Directions."
You should uphold it.
Furthermore, it is also titled "That Which Is Praised by the Tathāgata"; you should uphold it.
Furthermore, it is also titled "The Thorough Understanding of the Signless Dharma."
Furthermore, it is also titled ‘Emptiness and Non-existence’; one should diligently uphold it.
The Buddha told the youth:

“If there should be someone who receives this sutra, upholds, recites, and reads it, and explains it to others, fully and completely so that nothing is lacking, they will swiftly fulfill their aspirations.”
Bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who receive, uphold, recite, and read this sutra shall never have fear.
If they go before government officials, they will not be subjected to oppression or injustice;
if they travel among bandits, they will not be harmed.
If they walk through a great fire, it will be extinguished;
if they walk upon water, they shall never drown.
Whether gods, nāgas, ghosts and spirits, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, malevolent deities, or other various spirits—whether humans or non-humans—none dare to touch them.
Lions, tigers, wolves, fierce beasts, bears, and brown bears dared not approach;
hungry ghosts, *piśācas*, foot-reversing ghosts, and various ghosts from near latrines were unable to harass him, nor did he have anything to fear.
If one dwells in seclusion, in the wilderness, beneath a tree, or alone in the open air, one will be established by the Tathāgata and receive his protection.

If sons or daughters of good family receive this sutra, uphold it, recite it, read it, or transcribe it into a scroll, they have already made offerings to the Buddhas of the past, planted many roots of virtue, and their meritorious deeds are now about to be fulfilled.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Ānanda:

"Suppose there were someone who now beheld the Buddha face-to-face and, with a sincere heart, made offerings of robes, food and drink, bedding and furniture, and medicines for illness; this would not equal the merit of someone who receives, upholds, writes, recites, reads, records on bamboo or silk, and explains to others this sutra—such a person would thereby fully accomplish the offering to the Buddha."
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, arrived together with immeasurable devas, each bringing celestial flowers to scatter as an offering before the Buddha, and addressed him, saying:
"I shall protect and uphold those who maintain this sutra."
The Four Heavenly Kings and the various devas above each brought flowers and incense to make offerings to the Buddha, and each addressed the Buddha, saying:
“We shall protect and defend those sons and daughters of good family who receive this sutra, uphold it, recite it, read it, and explain it to others;

and for those who commit it to bamboo or silk and carry its scrolls, we shall provide protection and defense wherever they dwell or travel, ensuring that no one seeking an opportunity to harm them can find an opening.”

When the Buddha had spoken thus, the assembly of Śakra, the Lord of Devas; the youth Maitreya of the Śākya clan; the Four Heavenly Kings; and the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and humans of the world, having heard this sutra, rejoiced, paid homage, and withdrew.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Extinction of Darkness in the Ten Directions.
